Output exactly one raw JSON object. No markdown, no code fences, no prose.
Use schema keys exactly as written. Do not add, rename, omit, or reorder keys.

VALUE RULES
- Non-null values must be lowercase underscore_tokens.
- Scalars: one token or null.
- Arrays: unique tokens or [].
- Array fields are open-list: prefer known tokens when they fit, otherwise use a new concise token.
- When a detail token appears in exactly one CLOSED LIST, use that owner field; never repeat it across pattern, material, structure, or ornament.
- Each field must represent a single concept only.
- Do not combine multiple attributes into one token.

TAXONOMY
- item_type is only the game-data namespace; do not use it as visual evidence for category or subcategory.
- category = the broad visible object family, chosen at the schema root level rather than a more specific child type.
- category should be one of the values in CLOSED LISTS; use a new concise broad category only when no listed value fits the visible item.
- subcategory should be one primary, mutually exclusive object archetype directly under the chosen category, or null.
- Prefer the listed child examples when they fit, but subcategory is open-list.
- If no listed child term fits well, you may use a new concise child refinement or null.
- Unlisted categories and subcategories are flagged for registry review; use one only for a stable, clearly visible object family or archetype.
- subcategory should stay compatible with the selected category. If unsure, set subcategory = null.
- subcategory should name a type refinement, not a silhouette, material, pattern, color, length, haircut, texture, or other dedicated-field concept.
- Traits that can overlap with another archetype belong in their dedicated metadata fields, not in subcategory.
- Use an overlap test: if an item can have a distinction while also belonging to another child archetype, keep that distinction in metadata and choose only the primary archetype for subcategory.
- When a directly visible trait is not used as subcategory, still record it once in the appropriate metadata field; do not discard or duplicate it.
- A descriptive or culturally specific child name may still be valid when the whole term denotes a stable, visually recognizable object type rather than a detachable trait.

- Do not repeat category in subcategory.
- Do not compose multiple attributes into subcategory.
